HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. KOREAN FACES on everyone in frame: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, blue, grey or green, never the whole eyeball painted solid black); a low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European nose. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. KOREAN WEBTOON movie still, dramatic manhwa COVER. NOT photoreal. Dynamic dutch, FACES LARGE. Night Moon Palace yard. ONE device: a spear as a hard diagonal across the frame. LEFT of the sheet = Lady Chisul, FIFTIES, FACE from /ch_chisul.png, lined Korean face, grey at the temples, white jeogori black sash dark chima, mouth open screaming, arm grabbed by an unnamed Silla soldier, a small daughter lifted off the ground. Jesang a dark magenta back at the far third, NOT turning. One yard lamp. #c9a070 on her cheek. No young-girl Chisul. No text. No watermark. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = chisul, SECOND face = jesang. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: place board pl_moon_palace (keep this exact architecture and ground), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces). KOREAN FACES on every person, named or extra: living eyes with WHITE sclera, a small catchlight, and BLACK ink-black iris and pupil (never brown, hazel, amber, honey, gold, blue, grey, green or purple). Never paint the entire eyeball solid black. A low soft Korean nasal bridge, never a high European, Roman or Persian nose. East Asian bone: single-lidded or low-creased eyes, straight or softly arched brows, broad cheekbones, flatter facial planes, warm ivory to sun-browned skin, straight coarse black hair. Never Western, Latin, or mixed-race features, never deep-set double-lidded western eyes. LADY CHISUL — Look: Fifties, a lined Korean face, tired wanting eyes, long black hair with grey at the temples, worn up with a plain wooden binyeo. Dress: White silky jeogori, a black sash, a dark full chima (attached /ch_chisul.png). No gold, no crown. A south-shore wife’s dress. Colour #c9a070. PARK JESANG — Look: Fifties, long grey-white beard and moustache, silver at the temples, a calm half-lidded Korean face, hair in a high topknot. The south-shore Park who can fill a foreign hall. Dress: Magenta-plum silk po over a white inner collar and a dark navy jeogori (attached /ch_park_jesang.png). Bare head, no jougwan, no crown. Hands that have already decided. Colour #8B5A2B. PLACE Moon Palace (월성) — attached board /pl_moon_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Moon Palace (월성): Silla night court — timber halls, giwa roofs, packed-earth yards under moonlight, red pillars, a dark inner room with one lamp. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
